correctness.rationale: The paper-model minimal-recovery and exchange theorems are applied with their exact hypotheses. Over binary rank three, a minimal recovery subset must be independent, has at most three positions, and has XOR equal to a unit column; the verifier enumerates all such subsets exactly. Monotone peeling of all disjoint triples computes the greatest exchange-closed subfamily: every deletion is forced for all possible subfamilies, and a nonempty fixed point is itself exchange-closed. Complete enumeration of all 1716 seven-column and 3003 eight-column nonzero multisets yields respectively 0 and 79 admissible cores; zero-column removal and lengthening show the global length-8 minimum. All 79 literal strong recovery selections are checked for every disjoint partial history and all three next requests, with 17 orbit checks. The actual embedded verifier ran and returned VERIFY_OK. The only reliance on external theory is the proved, stated exchange characterization; no samples are mistaken for infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary paper already exhibits an eight-coordinate strongly-online generator (Example IV.22) but does not classify all minimum generator matrices or establish the seven-coordinate impossibility. The 2018/2022 original source formulates shortest lengths for small k among open directions and supplies broad constructions rather than this finite classification. Nearby public four-request binary batch results have different service models and do not imply the asynchronous three-request lower bound or 79-solution count. Searches of published research records and external literature did not find a dominating statement. Unindexed results may remain; absence of a search hit is not treated as novelty proof.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed or privately held exhaustive parameter table may cover the same classification.

value.rationale: This is a natural first nontrivial exact capacity and full optimizer classification for the explicitly studied 2026 asynchronous/strongly-online hierarchy at three requests: it distinguishes ordinary batch feasibility from asynchronous service, identifies sharp storage, exhibits 17 inequivalent named-message designs rather than only the previously known example, and proves every optimizer can use the stronger rule. It is not a renaming or routine corollary of the known eight-column construction. The finite parameter is mathematically motivated by the first case beyond the t<=2 general equivalence.
